title: C-O4 v2: `orchestrator serve` — bearer-authed HTTP API over goals (spec round 2 after T-0140; supersedes T-0116)
spec:
Why: the kgpt `modules/orchestrator` (Phase C, kgpt side) forwards start_goal/goal_status/list_goals/cancel_goal to a per-user endpoint; this is that endpoint, running in the executor container on the home network. Spec round 2: folds in spec review T-0140 (requester lives in goals.py, 409 via list_goals not string matching, sync handlers, full status-code map, explicit account field). Scope is 6 files by Planner decision: the requester field belongs in goals.py with its record, and README waits for the C-O5 runbook.

goals.py (small, additive): start(repo_path, goal_text, account_id="A", reinstall=False, requester=None) stores `requester` (string or None) on the goals.json record; _status_entry()/status()/list_goals() return it. Nothing else in goals.py changes. tests/test_goals.py: one test that start() with requester="alice" records it and status() returns it.

serve.py with starlette (import from the mcp dependency tree; if starlette or uvicorn is not importable, exit at startup with one line; do not add a dependency). All route handlers are plain `def` (not async) so starlette runs them in its threadpool: goals.start, git clone and goals.stop block for seconds and must not stall /healthz or other requests. Routes:
- GET /healthz (no auth) → 200 {"status": "ok"}.
- POST /goals body {repo, goal, requester, account?}: resolve slug via .orchestrator/repos.toml (slug → {path, git_url}); 404 {"reason": "unknown repo"} for an unknown slug; 400 when goal is empty or whitespace; when path is missing and git_url is set, `git clone <git_url> <ORCH_WORK>/<slug>` first (ORCH_WORK env, default /work; argv list, never a shell string; clone failure → 502 {"reason": "clone failed", "detail": stderr[-500:]}); BEFORE calling start, call goals.list_goals(path) and if any record has record_status == "running" and planner_alive is True → 409 {"reason": "goal already running", "goal_id": <id>}; then goals.start(path, goal, account_id=body.get("account", "A"), requester=body.get("requester")); launched true → 201 {goal_id, repo, status: "running", requester}; launched false → 422 {"reason": r["reason"]} (covers every precheck refusal incl. unknown account, staged changes, gitignored scaffold, missing planner.md); never a 500 for an expected refusal.
- GET /goals[?repo=slug] → 200 list from goals.list_goals per configured repo (all repos when no filter; 404 unknown slug).
- GET /goals/{repo}/{goal_id} → 200 goals.status(path, goal_id) entry, 404 when the repo or goal is unknown.
- POST /goals/{repo}/{goal_id}/cancel → goals.stop(path, goal_id); {"error": "unknown goal"} → 404; else 200 {goal_id, status: "stopped"}.
Auth: every route except /healthz requires `Authorization: Bearer <ORCH_SERVICE_TOKEN>` (env; the server refuses to start with one line and non-zero exit when unset), compared with hmac.compare_digest; 401 {"reason": "unauthorized"} otherwise. The token is never stored, logged or echoed; access log lines contain method, path, status only.
cli.py: `serve [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8090]` runs uvicorn with the app. `.orchestrator/repos.toml.example` with one commented entry showing slug, path, git_url.

Tests tests/test_serve.py with starlette's TestClient and goals.start/list_goals/status/stop patched (no real git): healthz_no_auth, rejects_missing_or_wrong_bearer, unknown_repo_404, empty_goal_400, start_returns_goal_id_and_requester (201; start called with requester and account kwargs), start_refusal_422 (start returns launched false → 422 with the reason), second_start_409_while_running (list_goals returns a running+alive record → 409 and start NOT called), cancel_marks_stopped, cancel_unknown_404, handlers_are_sync (assert no route endpoint is a coroutine function). No new dependency; finish with summary, files changed, failures-only test output; commit on the task branch when green.
acceptance: tests/test_serve.py has the ten named tests, green; tests/test_goals.py gains the requester test, green
goals.start accepts requester and status()/list_goals() return it; no other goals.py change (diff)
Every route handler is a plain def (no coroutine) and every start() refusal maps to 422 with the reason; 409 comes from list_goals, never from parsing start()'s reason string
`uv run orchestrator serve` without ORCH_SERVICE_TOKEN exits non-zero with one line; no route logs, stores or echoes the bearer
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green; no new dependency; only the six scoped files change; committed on the task branch

result.summary: superseded by C-O4 v3 (next task id after T-0143): spec review round 2 T-0143 requested changes (clone race needs a per-slug lock, module-attribute import for patching, slug on listing entries, requester type check). Specs are immutable on the bus, so recreated.

events.reason: Planner: killed a wrong-tool execute run before the spec review; requeued

spec_review_risks.issue: POST /goals clones on first use (path missing + git_url set) with no lock around the check-then-clone sequence. Route handlers run in starlette's threadpool specifically so concurrent requests aren't serialized, so two concurrent POST /goals for the same never-before-used slug can both observe 'path missing' and both exec `git clone` into <ORCH_WORK>/<slug> at once, corrupting the checkout or spuriously 502ing one of them. goals.py already has a precedent for this (GOALS_LOCK_NAME, _with_goals_lock) that serve.py should mirror per-slug before cloning.

Spec says tests patch 'goals.start/list_goals/status/stop' directly, but doesn't say serve.py must do `from . import goals` and call `goals.start(...)` through the module attribute. If it instead does `from .goals import start, list_goals, status, stop` (binding names at import time), `unittest.mock.patch` on `orchestrator.goals.start` etc. in test_serve.py will silently not intercept the calls serve.py makes, and the acceptance criterion 'no real git' / no real Popen spawn will fail in a confusing way.

GET /goals with no repo filter aggregates goals.list_goals(path) across every repo in repos.toml, but each entry's 'repo' field (from goals.json) is the absolute filesystem path on the executor box, not the repos.toml slug the kgpt caller knows. There's no way for the caller to map a multi-repo listing entry back to the slug it POSTed to /goals with unless it does prefix-matching against paths it was never given. Not covered by any named test, so this ships un-caught.

requester from the POST /goals body is passed straight into goals.start(..., requester=body.get('requester')) with no type check, but goals.py's contract for the new field is explicitly 'string or None'. Since kgpt-forwarded input is untrusted, a non-string requester (int/list/dict) gets written into goals.json and returned from status()/list_goals() unnormalized.
